decisions.statement: `--file-path` is named again for each file read.
A read returns the whole file or the difference after the agent read the file.
A read of a body the agent read already says so.
A body the agent's record already has comes back as one line saying so.
The difference comes back only where the difference is shorter than the whole file.
The difference is worked out against the body the record names and against no other body.
Where the body the agent read cannot be found again the whole file comes back and one line says why.
`--full` returns the body whatever the record has.
`--seat` is no argument a read takes, and saying it is refused with what it would mean.
A read of a body that is not UTF-8 text returns a description of the body instead of the body.
A body that would not open is refused with why that body would not.
A read takes no line range.
A read too big for one answer returns fewer files and how to ask for the rest.
A body past the bytes one answer has comes back a run of lines at a time.
A run of lines begins after the line the record has as read.
A body recorded as read in part is a body no record shows the agent read.
A body read in part whose bytes moved is begun again at its first line.
A body longer than one answer holds comes back alone.
A line no answer has room for is refused rather than divided.
No call returns a body past the bytes one answer has.
A read reaches no file outside this repository.
The line numbers a read prints are not part of the file.
The call for the rest is priced as that call is printed.
The call for the rest of a read naming no file is that read again.
A read records the body that reached the agent that read was for.
A read whose output is thrown away returns nothing and records nothing.
A read for an agent nothing identifies is refused.
A read is recorded beside the calling agent's own page.
A read waits for that page rather than answering a body it records nowhere.
A read waits 60 seconds for that page and goes the moment that page lands.
Each try of that wait reads the page index again rather than an answer held.
An agent whose page is already there waits not at all.
A read whose wait runs out is refused and answers no body.
That refusal tells the agent to change nothing and run the same call again.
A read whose wait runs out is an operational fault rather than a fault of input.
A read naming no file reads the calling agent's own seat page.
A subagent's own seat page is the page of the seat above that subagent.
An agent that has no seat page is refused with that as the reason.
That refusal says the agent was identified and the seat was not found.
A read naming no file hands back the files that seat page warrants.
A warrant reaches a read only where that warrant says that warrant runs on a read.
A file a warrant names is asked for files that file warrants only where the warrant is transitive.
A file the read reaches by two ways is one file in the answer.
A file a warrant names comes back after the file that warranted the named file.
A read the warrants cannot be worked out for returns the files the read was named.
Every answer here is built by a function rather than written out as a value.
A read naming a file that is not there is a fault of the input.
A read of a body that would not open is an operational fault.
A read naming a file hands back that file and no file that file warrants.
A file left over whose body the record already holds is neither counted nor named.

definition: the command returning each akasha file it is named, whole or as what changed since the agent read it

directives.name: One Read A Call
directives.act: Run one `akasha read` per shell call rather than chaining several into one.
directives.warrant: Output past what one shell result has is truncated, and the record still says it reached you.
aids: One call naming many files is safe; it caps itself.
The cap is per call, so chaining defeats it.
